title: sync-runtimehost-libs and Build-NpdevApp have different default -RuntimeHostLibsDir -- pass it explicitly to both
body:
After changing any kernel/adapter Java, you must restage jars before regenerating an app:

```powershell
scripts/runtimehost/sync-runtimehost-libs.ps1 -BuildLocalJars -RuntimeHostLibsDir D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\runtimehost-libs
```

The catch: `sync-runtimehost-libs.ps1`'s default libs dir does NOT match `Build-NpdevApp.ps1`'s default. If you let each use its own default, the sync writes fresh jars to one directory and the build reads stale jars from another -- the running app keeps the old jar and your change appears to have no effect. Always pass the SAME `-RuntimeHostLibsDir` to both. The `scripts/appgen/Rebuild-And-Restage.ps1` wrapper threads one shared dir through both and is the safe path.
